tracks.legalName: Automatic Annulment of a Non-Conviction Disposed of On or After January 1, 2019 (RSA 651:5, II-a(a))
tracks.publicName: Your dismissed or not-guilty New Hampshire case should clear itself

controllingAuthority.summary: New Hampshire calls this annulment, not expungement or sealing. Where a person is found not guilty on all charges that resulted from the arrest, or the case is dismissed or not prosecuted, and the offence was disposed of on or after January 1, 2019, the arrest record and court record shall be annulled thirty days after the finding if no appeal is taken under RSA 606:10, or on final determination of an appeal affirming the dismissal. There is no petition, no fee, no hearing and nothing to file. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: Offences disposed of before January 1, 2019, which need a petition under RSA 651:5, II.
A not-guilty finding on only some of the charges resulting from the arrest. The automatic route needs all of them.
Federal, military, tribal and out-of-state records. A New Hampshire annulment does not reach them and the federal government does not recognise it.

components.notes: The disposition-date screen. On or after January 1, 2019 routes here; before that date routes to the pre-2019 petition track. This single fact decides whether the participant is owed a free automatic annulment or needs to pay $125 to file, so it is asked first and answered from the court record rather than recollection.

How to confirm the annulment actually happened after the thirty days: request the New Hampshire criminal history from the State Police Criminal Records Unit on NHJB-2956, and check the case in the disposing court. Verify before assuming, because nothing arrives to tell the participant it worked.

What to do if the record still appears after the window. RSA 651:5 provides no express enforcement route, so the instruction is to raise it with the disposing court and the criminal records unit and to seek advice rather than to file a petition, and the packet says plainly that the remedy is not settled.

What annulment does and does not do, including the RSA 651:5, X(f) question form, law-enforcement retention under XI(b), sentencing and habitual-offender use, and the XVI and XVII rule that no one has to correct an earlier published report.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Annul the Record of a Non-Conviction Disposed of Before January 1, 2019 (RSA 651:5, II)
tracks.publicName: Annul an older New Hampshire arrest that did not end in a conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: A person found not guilty, or whose case was dismissed or not prosecuted, may petition at any time for annulment of the arrest record, the court record, or both, where the offence was disposed of before January 1, 2019 or otherwise falls outside the automatic route in paragraph II-a. Relief is discretionary under paragraph I: the court may annul if in its opinion the annulment will assist rehabilitation and be consistent with the public welfare, and it may grant or deny without a hearing unless the petitioner requests one. The court provides a copy of the petition to the prosecutor, who may be heard on the interest of justice, and the Department of Corrections performs a statutory investigation. RSA 651:5, IX and X(d) exempt a person found not guilty or whose case was dismissed or not prosecuted from the $100 Department of Corrections investigation fee and the $100 Department of Safety and state police fees. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: Offences disposed of on or after January 1, 2019, which are annulled automatically under RSA 651:5, II-a(a) with no petition and no fee.
Federal, military, tribal and out-of-state records.
A further petition within 3 years of a denial, barred by RSA 651:5, IV.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Annul the Record of a Vacated Conviction Outside the Automatic Route (RSA 651:5, II, second sentence)
tracks.publicName: Annul the record of a New Hampshire conviction that was vacated

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a criminal offence whose conviction was subsequently vacated by a court may petition for annulment where the offence falls outside the automatic route in paragraph II-a. There is no waiting period. Relief is discretionary under paragraph I and the court may decide without a hearing unless the petitioner requests one. The procedure, the form family, the investigation, the prosecutor's opportunity to be heard and the effect are the same as on the pre-2019 non-conviction petition; the difference is cost, because the RSA 651:5, IX and X(d) fee exemptions are written around not-guilty, dismissed and not-prosecuted cases and on the face of the statute do not reach a vacated conviction. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: Vacated convictions inside paragraph II-a, which are annulled automatically with no petition and no fee.
An order that is a reversal, a set-aside, a new trial order or a sentence modification rather than a vacatur.
Federal, military, tribal and out-of-state records.
A further petition within 3 years of a denial, barred by RSA 651:5, IV.

controllingAuthority.summary: New Hampshire calls this annulment of the record of arrest, conviction and sentence. A petition may be brought after the waiting period for the offence class has run from completion of all terms and conditions of the sentence, with no other conviction in that period except a motor vehicle violation other than DWI. Relief is discretionary: paragraph I lets the court annul if the annulment will assist rehabilitation and be consistent with the public welfare, and the court may decide without a hearing unless the petitioner requests one. Three rules make eligibility a whole-record question rather than a per-case one. Paragraph V bars any violent crime, any felony obstruction crime and any extended-term sentence outright. Paragraph VI forbids annulment where any part of the record is barred, or until the time requirements for all offenses of record have been met. Paragraph VIII dismisses a non-qualifying petition without a hearing, and paragraph IV then bars a further petition for three years. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: Any violent crime as defined by RSA 651:5, XIII: capital, first or second degree murder, manslaughter or class A felony negligent homicide under RSA 630; first degree assault under RSA 631:1; aggravated felonious sexual assault or felonious sexual assault under RSA 632-A; kidnapping or criminal restraint under RSA 633; class A felony arson under RSA 634:1; robbery under RSA 636; incest under RSA 639:2, III or endangering the welfare of a child by solicitation under RSA 639:3, III; and any felonious offense involving child sexual abuse images under RSA 649-A. RSA 651:5, V.

Any crime of obstruction of justice as defined by RSA 651:5, XIV: tampering with witnesses or informants under RSA 641:5, falsifying evidence under RSA 641:6, or any felonious offense of obstructing governmental operations under RSA 642. RSA 651:5, V.
Any offense for which the petitioner was sentenced to an extended term of imprisonment under RSA 651:6. RSA 651:5, V.

Any record where annulment of any part is barred under RSA 651:5, V, or where the time requirements under paragraphs III and IV have not been met for all offenses of record. RSA 651:5, VI freezes the whole record on one ineligible entry.
Impaired-driving convictions within RSA 265-A:21, which RSA 651:5, III excepts and which run on their own ten-year clock.
A further petition within 3 years of a denial. RSA 651:5, IV.
Federal, military, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Petition of Eligibility for Annulment of a Violation or Class B Misdemeanor Conviction, Streamlined Mandatory Route (RSA 651:5, III(a)(2) and III(b)(2))
tracks.publicName: The fast New Hampshire annulment route for a recent minor conviction

controllingAuthority.summary: For a violation or a class B misdemeanor with a conviction date on or after January 1, 2019 where that offence was the highest offense of conviction, the court submits a notice of its determination to the person and to the prosecutor. The prosecutor has twenty days from receipt to object, and only on two grounds: that the offence is not eligible for annulment, or that the person has not completed all the terms and conditions of the sentence. If no timely objection is made, or the objection is denied, the court shall annul the conviction. This is the only conviction route in New Hampshire where the paragraph I rehabilitation and public welfare discretion does not decide the outcome, and the only one with a defined objection clock and defined objection grounds. Paragraphs V, VI, VII and VIII still apply. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: A violation that is an offense specified under RSA 259:39, or another violation carrying an enhanced penalty for a subsequent conviction. Carved out of the violation row.
Sexual assault under RSA 632-A:4 and misdemeanor domestic violence under RSA 631:2-b. Carved out of the class B misdemeanor row.
Any offence that was not the highest offense of conviction in its case, which routes to the standard conviction route instead.
Convictions dated before January 1, 2019.

Any violent crime as defined by RSA 651:5, XIII: capital, first or second degree murder, manslaughter or class A felony negligent homicide under RSA 630; first degree assault under RSA 631:1; aggravated felonious sexual assault or felonious sexual assault under RSA 632-A; kidnapping or criminal restraint under RSA 633; class A felony arson under RSA 634:1; robbery under RSA 636; incest under RSA 639:2, III or endangering the welfare of a child by solicitation under RSA 639:3, III; and any felonious offense involving child sexual abuse images under RSA 649-A. RSA 651:5, V.

Any crime of obstruction of justice as defined by RSA 651:5, XIV: tampering with witnesses or informants under RSA 641:5, falsifying evidence under RSA 641:6, or any felonious offense of obstructing governmental operations under RSA 642. RSA 651:5, V.
Any offense for which the petitioner was sentenced to an extended term of imprisonment under RSA 651:6. RSA 651:5, V.

Any record where annulment of any part is barred under RSA 651:5, V, or where the time requirements under paragraphs III and IV have not been met for all offenses of record. RSA 651:5, VI freezes the whole record on one ineligible entry.
Impaired-driving convictions within RSA 265-A:21, which RSA 651:5, III excepts and which run on their own ten-year clock.
A further petition within 3 years of a denial. RSA 651:5, IV.
Federal, military, tribal and out-of-state records.

tracks.legalName: Petition of Eligibility for Annulment of the Record of Arrest or Conviction for Personal Possession of Marijuana (RSA 651:5-b)
tracks.publicName: Annul an old New Hampshire marijuana possession record

controllingAuthority.summary: A person arrested for or convicted of knowingly or purposely obtaining, purchasing, transporting or possessing, actually or constructively, or having under control, three quarters of an ounce of marijuana or less, where the offence occurred before September 16, 2017, may petition at any time for annulment of the arrest record, the court record, or both. The petition states that the amount was three quarters of an ounce or less. The petitioner, not the court, furnishes a copy to the office of the prosecutor of the underlying offence. The prosecutor may object within ten days of receipt and request a hearing; if no timely objection is made the court shall grant the petition, and if the prosecutor objects the court holds a hearing at which the prosecutor must prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the amount exceeded three quarters of an ounce, failing which the court shall grant the petition. If granted, RSA 651:5, X and XI apply in full. Under RSA 651:5, X(a) the person is treated in all respects as if never arrested, convicted or sentenced. Court records are sealed with the limited access list at X(c). The arresting and prosecuting agencies must clearly identify the annulment in their files and electronic records. Law enforcement retains records under XI(b) and may share them for legitimate investigative purposes, in defense of a civil suit arising from the arrest, and with the police standards and training council. A prior conviction may still be considered at sentencing on a later crime and may count toward habitual offender status under RSA 259:39. Under XVI and XVII no journalist, person or entity faces any penalty for publishing an annulled record or for not removing or correcting an earlier report, which is the statutory reason private background-check databases keep showing the case.

exclusions: Offences occurring on or after September 16, 2017, which are outside the section.
Any amount exceeding three quarters of an ounce.
Any offence involving sale, distribution or intent to distribute rather than the personal-possession verbs the section lists.

controllingAuthority.summary: RSA 265-A:21, I operates notwithstanding RSA 651:5, and RSA 651:5, III opens with an express exception for it. No court shall order annulment of a conviction for driving or attempting to drive a vehicle, for operating or attempting to operate or being in actual physical control of an OHRV, or for operating or attempting to operate a boat on New Hampshire waters, while under the influence or with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, or for aggravated drunken driving, until ten years after the date of conviction. The section was read at gc.nh.gov on 2026-08-06 and the clock runs from the date of conviction, not from completion of the sentence, which is different from every other New Hampshire conviction track. Any record annulled under the section shall be retained in a permanent file, to be opened only for purposes of sentencing in the case of an offence under RSA 265-A:3. Relief is discretionary under RSA 651:5, I once the ten-year bar has run; RSA 265-A:21 is a prohibition on early annulment, not a grant.

exclusions: Convictions within ten years of the date of conviction. RSA 265-A:21, I forbids the order outright.

tracks.legalName: Application to Annul a Conviction for Conduct at Age 17 Between May 14, 2014 and July 1, 2015 (RSA 651:5-a)
tracks.publicName: Annul an adult conviction for something you did at 17 during the transition period

controllingAuthority.summary: Any person convicted of a criminal offence which occurred between May 14, 2014 and July 1, 2015 while the person was 17 years of age shall be entitled to an annulment of that conviction upon application to the court. The only permitted basis for denial is a written finding by the court, on clear and convincing evidence, that the offence would have qualified for transfer to the superior court under RSA 169-B:24 and that the prosecution would have pursued such transfer. Annulment requests under the section are not subject to any filing fee. These are adult criminal convictions entered against people who were 17 during the window before New Hampshire raised the age of juvenile jurisdiction, so the records sit in the adult system and the relief belongs in ordinary adult scope. The section operates notwithstanding RSA 651:5, so the paragraph V bars and the paragraph VI whole-record rule appear not to apply, which if correct makes this the strongest relief in the state.
